clue.text: Rogue gets the armour-or gets the bearer

indicators.note: a rogue thing has gone wild and out of control, so the following letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A knave seizes a suit of armour, or seizes whoever carries it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the anagram signal working on GETS THE ARMOUR-OR, whose fifteen letters rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who carries a pregnancy for someone else is literally the one bearing the child.

clue.text: Pin's less symmetrical?

definitions.meaning: a long spike used to hold meat together while cooking

explanation.definitionFit: A kebab spike is a pin through meat, and 'skew' meaning askew takes the comparative ending to mean more lopsided.

clue.text: Woman's short strides

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: strides is British slang for trousers, here denim ones

explanation.surface: A lady's trousers are cut too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strides' is British slang for trousers; denim ones lose their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a common female first name.

clue.text: Having scrubbed seat, they finish soap

indicators.note: scrubbed suggests the word seat is scoured and roughed up into a new order

parts.note: those who finish things are enders

explanation.surface: Once the seat is cleaned, they wrap up the bar of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' looks like the cleaning bar to go with 'scrubbed', but it is a TV soap opera; EastEnders is the long-running BBC soap set in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running BBC television serial drama, the archetypal British soap opera.

clue.text: Colorant? David's new style encapsulates it with relevant sort of number

indicators.note: encapsulates means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other
a new style for the name David means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter
food ... carry E numbers, so E is the relevant kind of number

explanation.surface: A fashion note: David restyles his look to include something with the right number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new style' rearranges DAVID to ADDIV, which 'encapsulates' IT as ADD-IT-IV; E comes from the E numbers that label food additives in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A colouring agent is one kind of substance added to food, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Result of invalid claim

parts.note: reads as a rejected, void claim, but an invalid is an ill person claiming state payment for being unwell

explanation.definitionFit: State money paid to someone off work through illness is what an ill person's claim yields.

clue.text: Runaways abusing LSD are inspiring writer? …

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: cowards who run away are chickens

indicators.note: abusing means mistreating, so the letters of LSD and are get knocked about

explanation.surface: Teenage runaways taking drugs are the inspiration for a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runaways' are cowards, i.e. chickens. 'abusing' scrambles LSD and ARE into ARLESD; 'inspiring' (breathing in) holds it. The ellipsis carries the chickens into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist of Oliver Twist, whose own stories feature street runaways.

clue.text: With a sort of lunch, cook kicks and we punch

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or fiddle, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Over a light lunch, the chef kicks out and we throw a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' scrambles LUNCH with KICKS AND WE; the answer is British slang for a punch in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a blow to the face, the fist being served up like a snack.

clue.text: … Unofficial advisers have bitten one of them off!

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of place, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: one of the runaways from the previous clue, which were chickens: a chicken

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: the shadow advisers have had a bite of one of the chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' points back across the ellipsis to the chickens of 7 Down, so 'one of them' is A CHICKEN; 'off' scrambles that with BITTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader's informal circle of confidants, as opposed to the official ministers, gets this domestic label.

clue.text: Way to restart sport or get Boat Race day abandoned repeatedly?

indicators.note: abandoned twice over: each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: on Boat Race day the event is simply the rowing

explanation.surface: Ask how play resumes, or how to get the Oxford-Cambridge race called off again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames. 'abandoned repeatedly' docks the last letter of THE and of ROWING.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby, play restarts from the touchline by a ball being hurled back onto the pitch.

clue.text: In there, unfulfilled writer gives rendition of Il Penseroso

indicators.note: put in, so one piece sits inside the other
not completed, so the word there loses a letter

parts.note: ink stands for what a writer puts on the page

explanation.surface: Within it, a frustrated poet performs Milton's meditative poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfulfilled' drops the last E of THERE; 'In' holds the ink. Il Penseroso, Milton's poem, means 'the pensive man' in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title means the pensive or contemplative man, someone deep in thought.

clue.text: Horrible hero puts jelly on Henry

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
agar is a jelly made from seaweed

explanation.surface: A ghastly champion pours jelly over a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Hagar the Horrible is a Viking cartoon strip, so 'Horrible' is part of his title, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: The Viking title character of a comic strip, Hagar the Horrible.

clue.text: Creature inept divers give skins?

indicators.note: skins means covers the outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to give up or yield is to cede

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various or diverse, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Clumsy scuba divers hand over their wetsuits to some animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like underwater swimmers but means diverse, scrambling INEPT to NTIPE, which CEDE 'skins'.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-legged arthropod is one kind of living thing.

clue.text: One of the writers reassigned to trenches

indicators.note: reassigned means given new places, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: One author has been posted off to the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is G.K. Chesterton; the trenches and reassignment suggest a war poet.
explanation.definitionFit: G.K. Chesterton, the English author of the Father Brown stories, is one such literary figure.

clue.text: Reclining woman of the night in a German compound

indicators.note: lying back, so in a horizontal answer the whole run reads backwards
one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ein is German for a
a tart is a prostitute

explanation.surface: A prostitute lies back in a German compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reclining' reverses the whole container, so it reads backwards in the across grid; tart as 'woman of the night' is a common crossword euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt of nitric acid is one chemical compound.

clue.text: Deny poor Ben looks stoned!

indicators.note: Ben looks out from within, so his letters are set inside the other piece

parts.note: agate is a stone, the one Ben is set in

indicators.note: poor means badly done, so the letters of Ben are jumbled

explanation.surface: Turn down poor Ben, who seems to be high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' suggests drugs, but it means set in stone; 'poor' jumbles BEN to BNE, which 'looks' out from inside the gem.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse oneself something is a formal way of saying deny.

clue.text: Endlessly where you'd want to live with me, going back above the surface of the water

definitions.text: above the surface of the water

indicators.note: going back means the joined pieces are read in the opposite direction
without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: des res is estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dream home where one would like to settle, rising out of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: DES RES, British estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence, loses its last letter ('Endlessly'); add ME and 'going back' turns DESREME round.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for leaves or plants standing out of the water rather than submerged.

clue.text: Fossils? Old wicket-keeper has money on it

indicators.note: has means holds within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Les Ames kept wicket for Kent and England in the 1930s
M is used for money, as in the economists' money-supply measures M0 and M1
taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired cricketer has placed a bet on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like it describes the fossils, but belongs to the cricketer: a wicket-keeper stands behind the stumps, and Les Ames played for England before the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Coiled shells of extinct sea creatures are common fossil finds; the question mark admits they are one example.

clue.text: I like a cuppa — apparently the reason for thinner polar bears?

indicators.note: made thinner, so the frozen surface loses a letter

parts.note: polar bears live and hunt on sea ice

explanation.surface: A tea lover explains that drinking tea is apparently why polar bears are getting skinnier.
explanation.walkthrough: THE plus ICE made 'thinner' by losing its E: melting sea ice is the real reason polar bears go hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for someone addicted to drinking tea, a cup of which is a cuppa.

clue.text: One bird or more is able to hear it

indicators.note: to hear it means the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: more than one is two, and is able is can

explanation.surface: Whether one bird or many, it is capable of hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: After 'One', 'more' means two: 'two can' is said exactly like the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical bird with a huge bright beak.

clue.text: A whole genre is going mad with it

indicators.note: going mad means losing order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An entire literary genre loses its mind over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is going mad' scrambles GENRE with IT; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians call a whole number with no fraction part by this name.

clue.text: Some sleep required, yet he gets us aroused

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: He needs a nap, yet he keeps us awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aroused' stirs up YET HE with US. The surface talks of waking, the answer of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal for a nap, a bit of rest with closed eyelids.

clue.text: Sauce? Say nothing in jest

indicators.note: in jest means playfully, so the letters are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A cheeky retort, said only as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks like cheek, matching 'jest', but it is the condiment made from the bean.
explanation.definitionFit: The bean from which a salty Asian condiment is brewed; the question mark covers the shortening.

clue.text: In which the motion has current consideration?

definitions.text: In which the motion has current consideration?

parts.words: In which the motion has current consideration?
parts.note: reads as a debate where a motion is topical, but means the physics of moving electric currents

explanation.definitionFit: The branch of physics dealing with electric currents and the forces of moving charges.
